case_name: G. Valli Alias Rayaprolu vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Anr.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: G. Valli Alias Rayaprolu, major daughters of the declarant
parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Andhra Pradesh And Anr., declarant (surplus holder)

facts_of_case: Declarant declared as surplus holder; daughters claimed share in property on par with sons due to Hindu Succession Act amendment; requested exclusion of their shares from holding.

legal_principles.principle: Daughters are entitled to claim shares in the joint family property on par with brothers.
legal_principles.held: The daughters are entitled to claim shares in the joint family property on par with the brothers.
cited_cases: Kum. Addalagadda Alivelamma v. Special Tahasildar, (1987) 2 APLJ (HC) 192

legal_principles.principle: A family unit consisting of five members is entitled to one standard holding, and every member in excess of five is entitled to possess 1/5th of the standard holding.
legal_principles.held: A family unit consisting of five members is entitled to one standard holding and every member in excess of five is entitled to possess 1/5th of the standard holding.
applicable_acts_sections: Andhra Pradesh Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act — Section 4

outcome.final_order: Order passed by the Appellate Tribunal not accepted, and declarant declared as non-surplus holder.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Succession Act implications
